'''Abran Balfour''' was the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Imperial]] [[Moff/Legends|Moff]] of the [[Parmic sector/Legends|Parmic sector]], whose forces constantly patrolled the [[Llanic Spice Run/Legends|Llanic Spice Run]]. Balfour operated from a fortress at the [[Space station/Legends|space station]] [[Spice Terminus/Legends|Spice Terminus]], where he kept a private collection of exotic [[Sentience/Legends|non-sentient]] [[Species/Legends|species]]. Derided as an inefficient and apathetic [[Governor/Legends|governor]], Balfour was less interested in [[Politics/Legends|political]] and military matters than he was with restoring the vintage [[Freighter/Legends|space barge]] known as the ''[[Lady Telura]]''. The restoration led him to pursue rare [[Starship/Legends|ship]] parts, and he found himself in contact with organizations such as [[The Most Honourable Guild of Armourers]]. Due to his unorthodox order of priorities, Moffs of bordering [[Sector/Legends|sectors]] constantly criticized Balfour, though his lax attitude alone left him bereft of true enemies.

He soon became notorious for his attitude, and was the subject of several political songs, "[[Moff Balfour's Lament (Tapmint Surprise)]]" among them. Nonetheless, he was undeterred, and had the utmost faith in the security of his sector. Eventually, his faith was shaken when Parmic became a nexus of Imperial activity following reported [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel]] strikes and rumors of a [[Mandalorian/Legends|Mandalorian]] presence in the sector. Eventually, Balfour was deposed by a [[Mercenary/Legends|mercenary]] group, the [[Laramus Base Irregulars]]. His holdings were later investigated by operatives working for the ascendant [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]].

==Biography==
===Moff of the Parmic sector===
Due to his complete lack of [[Politics/Legends|political]] knowledge, and the fact that he was bereft of charisma, [[Moff/Legends|Moff]] Abran Balfour was relegated to controlling the backwater [[Parmic sector/Legends|Parmic sector]] for the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]]. Balfour [[Governor/Legends|governed]] the [[Sector/Legends|sector]] from the [[Space station/Legends|space station]] [[Spice Terminus/Legends|Spice Terminus]], where he had a private fortress. There, he kept a wide collection of rare and exotic [[Sentience/Legends|non-sentient]] [[Species/Legends|creatures]].<ref name="trg">''[[Star Wars: The Roleplaying Game, Second Edition, Revised and Expanded]]''</ref>

Instead of properly governing the sector, Balfour preferred to ignore enemy activity and work on restoring the vintage [[Thalassia/Legends|Thalassian]] [[Freighter/Legends|space barge]] ''[[Lady Telura]]''. The [[Starship/Legends|ship]] was a rare model and required an assortment of very rare parts in order to be properly restored. Balfour would often journey far from the sector [[Capital/Legends|capital]] hunting for parts to restore the ship, and would enlist the help of [[The Most Honourable Guild of Armourers]] in his search. If he ever needed to return to the Parmic sector, his position afforded him a fast ship in case of emergency, although Balfour was usually warned well in advance if a situation arose. Due to his shifted priorities, Balfour was more than happy to let the [[Planet/Legends|planetary]] governors do their work with little guidance from him.<ref name="gg9" />

===Moff Balfour's lament===
[[File:Elena_Shelvay.jpg|180px|thumb|Balfour's aide Elena Shelvay secretly worked for the ISB.]]
During this time, according to [[Galactic Weekly NewsStack]], Balfour managed to start a [[Gamorrean/Legends|Gamorrean]] clan war by uttering the word "oink," which, unbeknownst to the Moff, was a deadly insult in their [[Gamorrese|native tongue]]. He was also the target of political protest songs from the banned [[Music/Legends|musical]] groups "[[Red Shift Limit/Legends|Red Shift Limit]]" and "[[Deeply Religious]]," who released "[[Moff Balfour's Lament (Tapmint Surprise)]]."<ref name="gg9" /> Security in certain parts of the sector was so lax that at one stage that Balfour's undergarments were apprehended by an ordinance procurer.<ref name="hr" /> His ineptitude was such that [[Smuggler/Legends|smuggling]] became an easy option for criminals in the Parmic sector, and some believed that the Moff simply had no idea how to do his job.<ref name="pap">''[[Pirates & Privateers]]''</ref> When the issue of [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Alliance to Restore the Republic]] activity in his sector was raised, Balfour would dismiss it, choosing to ignore such a possibility in the hope that it would subside.<ref name="gg9" />

Since the [[Troop/Legends|troops]] under Balfour's command were well equipped, they were able to keep the sector relatively free of Rebel operations despite his lack of participation. His forces constantly patrolled the [[Llanic Spice Run/Legends|Llanic Spice Run]], which was the only locale of note in the sector. While his apathy gained him few supporters, Balfour likewise had very few enemies, save for the Moffs of neighboring sectors who thought that his laid back ''modus operandi'' could be dangerous. Balfour was also apparently under surveillance from the [[Imperial Security Bureau/Legends|Imperial Security Bureau]], who had inserted their agent, [[Elena Shelvay]], as one of the Moff's aides.<ref name="gg9" />

===Collapse of the Empire===
Content that his sector was secure from Rebel activity, Balfour's seemingly easy job became very difficult in short order, due to staff incompetence, Rebel coordination, and rumors of a [[Mandalorian/Legends|Mandalorian]] [[Battlecruiser/Legends|battlecruiser]] adrift in the area. Soon, the Parmic sector was alive with Imperial activity, and was deemed a "danger zone."<ref name="gg9" /> Eventually, [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Galactic Emperor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]] died at the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|Battle of Endor]], and those left with power on [[Coruscant/Legends|Imperial Center]] found themselves squabbling for total dominion over the now fragmented Empire.<ref name="nec">''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''</ref> The militant [[Mercenary/Legends|mercenary]] group known as the [[Laramus Base Irregulars]] were able to topple Balfour's control over the Parmic sector, and soon after, [[Voren Na'al/Legends|Voren Na'al]], a historian working for the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]], was sent to peruse the former Moff's records at the Spice Terminus fortress. In doing so, he activated one of Balfour's traps, but emerged unscathed.<ref name="trg" />

==Personality and traits==
{{Quote|Rebel activity? In my sector? Ignore it and it will go away.|Abran Balfour|<ref name="gg9" />}}
Abran Balfour differed from his colleagues in that he maintained an unkempt appearance, lacked charisma, was unfit, and was notably poor at politics. As such, he was relegated to the backwater Parmic sector. Personally, Balfour saw himself as a knowledgeable historian, and an able politician. Conversely, he was unable to gain the respect of the Imperial troops under his command, a situation that proved disastrous when the Parmic sector garnered Alliance attention. Even when it did, Balfour had an apathetic stance toward the threat and would always caution his men to ignore any dissident activity.<ref name="gg9" />

He was more than happy to shun his responsibilities and let the planetary governors operate, while he hunted for spare parts in his restoration of the vintage [[Realspace/Legends|space]] barge, the ''Lady Telura''. He was highly confident in the security of his sector;<ref name="gg9" /> a confidence that would prove unfounded when his undergarments were stolen.<ref name="hr" /> In fact, security was so lax under Balfour's supervision that a life of crime was considered a natural and easy one in the Parmic sector.<ref name="pap" /> Balfour also had a great interest in non-sentient animals, and had a vast collection kept in a private [[Zoo/Legends|zoo]] at the Spice Terminus fortress. The zoo was also heavily booby trapped&mdash;a fact discovered by the curious New Republic agent Voren Na'al.<ref name="trg" />

==Behind the scenes==
Abran Balfour was created as a character in [[1993]]'s ''[[Galaxy Guide 9: Fragments from the Rim]]'', a roleplaying supplement written by [[Simon Smith]] and [[Eric S. Trautmann]] as part of [[West End Games]]' ''[[Star Wars: The Roleplaying Game]]''.<ref name="gg9" />
